brief: Goldman's Coppersmith argues the weekend's AI news lands on a market that had just re-exposed itself to tech. GS Prime Brokerage shows hedge funds bought US TMT in 10 of the last 11 sessions, a two-week buying pace in the 97th percentile of five years, and then Dario pushed for a slower pace of frontier-model development. Factor volatility already runs far above index volatility, 200-day vol of about 76 on GS TMT momentum winners versus losers against about 13 for the SPX, and the GS Panic Index fell 3 points Friday, so less index fear is priced against those rebuilt longs. Against that, conference messaging was strong. Jensen reiterated $3-4tn of AI infrastructure spend by 2030, with power, land and datacenter capacity the bottleneck rather than demand, so the note reads the concern as AI moving too fast rather than demand disappointing. The second risk is Iran plus rates, with the 10-year pushing toward 5% and the S&P forward multiple already down from about 22x to about 19x. GIR expects a 25bp hike next week because the market forced the Fed's hand, not because inflation deteriorated. Near-term volatility yes, a break in the AI story no.
